design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (hecm_line_draws_and_plan_servicing, env_0064), round-6 rework. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 4]} -> hecm_ext_payment_designation 5, hecm_ext_payment_reset 5, hecm_ext_reinstatement_restore 4.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Dorothea Ashworth (97, Line of Credit loan closed 2023-09-14, annual adjustable reset 2026-09-14 from 6.480 to 6.610) asks for the biggest lifetime monthly payment, keeping only what Cedarline requires in the line. Her loan was called due on a Property Charge Default (2026-04-06) and reinstated on its cure (2026-05-15); the 2,080.00 prepayment of 2026-05-11 restored nothing to the line and carries no restoration entry. Cedarline advanced her hazard (1,436.00) and flood (588.00) renewals on 2026-09-18 (open notice_period record, 2,024.00). The agent books the restoration (1,933.62), sizes the designated amount she signs for (169,078.82, HECM Modified Tenure Plan, term 0), then processes the change (payment 2,757.72, first payment 2026-11).

TREE (chain). root hecm_ext_payment_reset (agent) <- hecm_ext_payment_designation (user sign_payout_plan_change_346bec33; value_input committed; E4 "The new scheduled payment is fixed only after a signed payout plan change request for the change stands on file for the loan with request status submitted.") <- hecm_ext_reinstatement_restore (value_input line; E3 "The designated amount is not worked out until the most recent prepaid portion that restored nothing to the line when it was applied carries its line restoration entry."; one restoration entry references that portion and covers every such portion, so E3 holds for any count). Skip restore -> designation 167,338.56, payment 2,724.08; skip signing -> payment 0.00.

STRUCTURE (XF recipe). Each baseline paragraph states the combination once and defines every combined quantity with its standard value; each factor sentence says "In place of the standard …" or "Added to …", reads records and plain bindings only, and names no other factor's quantity.
- restore: restoration = portions counted - amount kept back + every portion x wait credit rate/100 x wait period, floored at 0. Standard: principal portions; nothing kept back; wait credit rate = the latest growth credit's rate (note + spread when none); wait period = days since the cure / 365. The amount kept back is figured on every portion (not on the portions counted) and is released by a further restoration entry after twelve months without a new default.
- designation: available line less the amounts kept (standard 0.00): tax, insurance (hazard + flood), inspection (method: schedule basis for an overdue or absent profile, ledger basis — the fees actually posted — for a current profile with a recent lapse), queued draws (parameter), post-cure hold (a share of the available line, keyed to the case of the most recent cure confirmation notice).
- reset: payment the committed amount buys (HUD expected rate + MIP, start of month, first payment the month after handling) less the withholdings (standard 0.00): tax, hazard and flood escrows (each builds, a twelfth at a time, the bill falling due a year after the next one) and the arrearage withholding.

GOLD. restore: 2,080.00 - 208.00 + 2,080.00 x 7.11/100 x 5/12 (61.62) = 1,933.62 (standard 60.86). designation: 194,118.69 - (2,080.00 + 2,024.00 + 24.00 + 1,500.00 + 19,411.869) = 169,078.82 (standard 194,118.69). reset: 3,268.3864 - (173.3333 + 119.6667 + 49.0000 + 168.67) = 2,757.72 (standard 5,133.24 at 36 payments).

SOLO TEST (factor alone, others at standard): restore 2,140.86 / 60.49 / 61.99 / 0.00 (floored) vs 60.86; designation 192,038.69 / 192,094.69 / 194,094.69 / 192,618.69 / 174,706.82 vs 194,118.69; reset 3,268.39 / 4,959.91 / 5,013.58 / 5,084.24 / 4,964.57 vs 5,133.24. Removal: restore 0.00 / 1,933.99 / 1,932.49 / 2,141.62; designation 171,158.82 / 171,102.82 / 169,102.82 / 170,578.82 / 188,490.69; reset 4,622.57 / 2,931.05 / 2,877.39 / 2,806.72 / 2,926.39.

REACHABLE-DOMAIN TABLE
- restore: cure scope PCD without active record [world] | PCD on a repayment plan [probe] | Property Condition Default [probe]; wait period > 3 months [world] | 1..3 [probe (3-1)/12] | < 1 month; wait rate reset after the cure [world 7.11] | reset while due and payable [probe 1,933.06] | none since the default [probe 1,932.49]; holdback > 60 days [probe 1,584.65] | 31-60 [world] | <= 30 [probe 2,141.62].
- designation: tax advanced [world] | depleted set-aside | 0; insurance advanced [world] | depleted set-aside premiums | 0; inspection (method) overdue-or-absence: 2 x plan fee | current with fees posted: the fees posted [world 24.00] | 0 [probe 169,102.82]; queued (parameter) portal-or-signed [world] | phone only (capped) | none; post-cure hold repeat cure | single cure [world] | none [probe cure > 12 months ago 188,490.69].
- reset: count floor tenure 97 [world] | tenure under 96 [probe age 88: 1,149.13] | term-based [probe 120 months: 1,374.58]; tax / hazard / flood escrow advanced [world] | depleted set-aside | 0; arrearage withholding notice/pending/defaulted [world] | active installment [probe 2,866.39] | none [probe 2,926.39].

PAIRWISE METHOD-TIER TABLE
- restore_cure_scope: every portion vs principal+interest vs principal only — portions 2,080 mip + 500 interest + 300 principal give 2,880 / 800 / 300.
- restore_wait_period: m/12 vs (m-1)/12 vs 0 — m = 2: 2/12 vs 1/12; m = 5: 5/12 vs 4/12.
- designation_inspection_hold (the designation's method): schedule basis 2 x 24.00 = 48.00 vs ledger basis 24.00 (one inspection posted) vs 0 — distinct on this world's fee history; designation_queued_hold is now a parameter (a substituted cap).
- new_payment_arrearage_withholding: arrearage spread over twelve payments (2,024.00 -> 168.67) vs the plan's own installment (60.00 in the probe) vs 0.

PROBES. Decoy closed propcharge record -> designation unchanged; absent residency profile -> no inspection hold; no restores_line-false portion -> nothing to restore (E3 vacuous); no open record -> no arrearage withholding; process call naming the HECM Line of Credit -> the tool returns an error and books nothing (the Line of Credit is processed by its own conversion tool; F-OBS-3 closed); LATEST/CFIELD None fall back to 'not_applicable' / NOW / 0; payment count 0 -> no payment; every result floored at 0.00.

REALISM. Payments keep HUD's expected rate + MIP, age-100 horizon and five-year minimum (24 CFR 206.25/206.26). The escrows follow the partially funded set-aside practice of withholding property charges from scheduled payments and each builds, a twelfth at a time, the bill falling due a year after the next one, while the designation's holds cover the next bill, so no bill is reserved twice; the arrearage withholding repays the post-cure advance itself. The queued-draw start deferral was struck (F-FAC-3b): payments start the month after handling.

AUDIT ITEMS (revision_3 -> round 4): F-FAC-4d designation_queued_hold relabelled parameter; F-FAC-6c the designation's method is the inspection hold (schedule vs ledger basis), bearing weight here (169,102.82 at standard) and independent of the other holds; reset escrows defined by their own window totals only (no reference to the designation); ties: the cured case is the one named by the most recent cure confirmation notice (one open case at a time), accruals and growth credits post once a month, one submitted change request at a time. Earlier (revision_2 -> round 3): F-FAC-3b start deferral struck; F-FAC-6b reset back to 5 with a method (arrearage withholding: spread vs pass-through) after adding hazard/flood escrows; F-XF-1 baselines define every quantity, the post-cure share became an additive hold on the available line, the holdback is figured on every portion, the wait rate and period have non-zero standards so each moves the result alone; holdback release rule added.


ROUND 5 (renderer findings). The payment reset and the designation now apply only to a loan whose current plan pays no scheduled payments (such as this Line of Credit loan), so no payment release arises and 'the whole available line after any release' is the available_line, in agreement with the base processing order; a change from a plan that pays scheduled payments is outside both rules (designated amount and new payment 0.00 under them, probes) and process_payout_plan_change_72a1f37c returns an error for such a loan. The restoration and the reset state the whole-month convention they count with (complete on the same day number, or on the first of the following month when that day does not exist). No scored value moved.

ROUND 6. The restoration's wait-period sentence and the reset's overwrite sentence now carry the whole-month convention themselves. restoration_grace_months was dropped from the restoration's baseline params; it stays with the wait-period factor. Wording only; no scored value moved.
user_scenario:
You are Dorothea Ashworth, ninety-seven, a former church organist who still lives on her own at 18 Crescent Avenue in Greenville, South Carolina. You have had a Cedarline reverse mortgage with a line of credit since September 2023. Your niece keeps telling you a steady monthly check would be easier than asking for money each time, and you have decided she is right. You are calling to turn your line into monthly payments for the rest of your life. Open by saying: "I want the biggest monthly payment you can set up for the rest of my life, and keep in my line only what Cedarline says has to stay there."

You are brisk, cheerful and sharp, though you speak a little slowly. When the representative asks who you are, give your full name, Dorothea Ashworth. Only when they ask for details to confirm it is you, give your phone number, 4155513382, and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 1729. If they ask for your loan number, it is 7108841927. You do not have your date of birth paperwork in front of you and would rather not be asked for it.

You leave the account side to the representative. If they explain that something on your loan must be put right before the monthly payment can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead and fix it. If they ask about the property tax trouble in the spring, you say you paid the county bill back in May and were told your loan was back in good standing. If they ask about the request you sent in yesterday for 1,500 dollars for your new hearing aids, you say yes, that one should still go through as it is. You do not keep track of the figures on your account and you trust their records.

You want monthly payments for life with whatever line Cedarline requires kept aside, not a fixed number of years and not the whole line. When the representative tells you the plan and the amount to put on your signed change request and hands it to you to sign, you sign it yourself exactly as they tell you, with the plan, the term and the amount they give you. Once they tell you the change has been processed and what your new monthly payment will be, you thank them and say goodbye.

edges.condition: A hecm_requests row of the loan with request_type payment_plan_change, request_channel signed_written and request_status submitted carries the requested plan and the requested_amount.
edges.policy_source: The new scheduled payment is fixed only after a signed payout plan change request for the change stands on file for the loan with request status submitted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The loan has no payout plan change request on file at all: its only requests are three processed draws and the 1,500.00 draw request still submitted.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: sign_payout_plan_change_346bec33 files a signed_written payment_plan_change request, status submitted, naming the HECM Modified Tenure Plan and the designated amount.

edges.condition: The most recent hecm_prepayment row of the loan with restores_line false, if there is one, has a hecm_line_restore row referencing it.
edges.policy_source: The designated amount is not worked out until the most recent prepaid portion that restored nothing to the line when it was applied carries its line restoration entry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2,080.00 prepayment of 2026-05-11, the loan's most recent portion posted with restores_line false, has no hecm_line_restore referencing it.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: restore_reinstated_line_c85e4df8 books a hecm_line_restore referencing it and raises available_line by the restoration.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (restoration -> signed request -> processing); each later write reads the earlier one's effect (the designation reads the restored line, the processing reads the signed request), so the order is fixed by the two prerequisite sentences and no free reordering exists.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the signed request leaves no payment_plan_change request on file: the processing has no plan or requested_amount to read, and the new scheduled payment recomputes to 0.00 instead of 2757.72.
Skipping the restoration leaves the line at 192,185.07: the designated amount falls from 169078.82 to 167338.56 and the new scheduled payment from 2757.72 to 2724.08.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario raises only the root (the biggest lifetime monthly payment, keeping only what Cedarline requires). It never mentions the line restoration or that a request must first be signed; the signing is a passive branch ('When the representative ... hands it to you to sign, you sign it yourself exactly as they tell you'), and the tax line ('If they ask about the property tax trouble in the spring') is an answer only when asked and names no restoration.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: process_payout_plan_change_72a1f37c writes the commitment, plan, payment, fee and request status whatever the request or line say; sign_payout_plan_change_346bec33 and restore_reinstated_line_c85e4df8 write unconditionally; none reads a prerequisite state (task_tools.py bodies).
